Paula, I have a question. How did you come to Zurich? Did you apply?
No, I didn't apply. Sofia called me.
Really? So you didn't look for the job. When did she call you?
In March, last year. I didn't know the company. A broker gave her my name.
And the interview? Were you nervous?
Very nervous. I didn't sleep the night before. Not one hour.
I know that feeling. What did they ask you?
They asked about large risks for twenty minutes. They didn't ask about my English. Not one question.
That doesn't surprise me. Did they hire you that week?
They sent the offer two weeks later. But I didn't decide that day. I took a week.
Why did you say yes in the end?
Because they didn't want perfect English. They wanted a real story. And I had one.

Hi, Paula. David here. Today you are going to learn the small word that changes everything in the past, and it is didn't. Before your lesson, let me tell you what I didn't do. Ten years ago, a big company in Chicago called me for an interview. I didn't apply for that job. They found me. And here is my confession. The night before, I didn't sleep. Not one hour. I was nervous, and I made a long list of hard words in English, because I thought they were going to test my grammar. Then I sat down in that room, and they didn't ask about my grammar. They didn't ask about my list. They asked one question. Tell us about a problem you solved. So I told them a story about a client, in simple words, with many mistakes, and they hired me two days later. I didn't win that job with perfect English, Paula. I won it with a real story. Remember one thing today. After didn't, the verb goes back to normal. I didn't sleep. I didn't apply. Never I didn't slept. The past is already inside the word didn't, so the verb does not repeat it. That is the whole rule. See you soon.

Good morning, Paula. Sofia here. Last year I was in the room when you came for your interview at Zurich, and today I want to tell you what happened on our side of the table, because I don't think you know. First, you didn't apply for that job. We called you. A broker in Sao Paulo said your name to me, and I looked for you. Second, you arrived early, and you were nervous. I saw it. Your hands were nervous, but your voice was not. You talked about large risks for twenty minutes and you didn't stop once. And now the part I really want you to hear. We didn't ask about your English. Not one question. Two of the people at that table asked me later, is her English good? And I said, I don't know, and it is not the reason we want her. We hired you because you know the work, and because you didn't pretend. When you didn't have a number, you said, I will check and come back. Do you know how rare that is? So today, when you learn didn't, think about this. You didn't get this job because you were perfect. You got it because you were honest, and you did not stop. See you Monday, Paula.
